knowledge:
- key_parameters: coverage=Minimum coverage threshold for extracting methylation per SNP in extract_bams ;; pvalAssign=Method to calculate cluster p-values in find_dames, either "Simes" (default, clusters by closeness) or "empirical" (bumphunting with permutations) ;; maxGap=Maximum distance between CpG sites to be clustered in find_dames ;; smooth=Logical parameter in find_dames to smooth moderated t-statistics ;; plotSNP=Logical parameter in dame_track to plot the SNPs involved in the ASM calculation ;; window=Number of CpG positions to add to the plot up and down-stream in dame_track ;; positions=Number of base pairs to add to the plot up and down-stream in dame_track
- alternatives: bismark_methylation_extractor=Standard tool for methylation calls, but extract_bams is preferred here because it specifically extracts allele-specific methylation for CpG sites falling within reads containing a heterozygous SNP ;; methtuple=External tool used to generate tuple files for the fast-mode workflow ;; Bis-SNP=Recommended for variant calling from bisulfite-converted reads to obtain the VCF file needed for the SNP-based mode
- when_to_use: Use when analyzing bisulfite-sequencing (BS-seq) data across multiple samples to detect loss or gain of allele-specific methylation (e.g., genomic imprinting, X chromosome inactivation, or cancer-related loss of imprinting). Use the SNP-based mode when interested in sequence-dependent ASM linked to heterozygous SNPs. Use the tuple-based mode when SNP information is unavailable, or for exploratory analysis of intermediate methylation levels representing ASM.
- pitfalls: SNP-based mode requires a VCF file with heterozygous SNPs per sample; without it, the tuple-based mode must be used. For the tuple-based mode, BAM files must be sorted by query name (samtools sort -n) before running methtuple. The empirical p-value assignment method (pvalAssign = "empirical") in find_dames can take longer depending on the number of samples and permutations. Ensure the colData of the SummarizedExperiment contains group and samples columns before running dame_track.

workflows.name: snp_based_dame_detection
workflows.intent: Extract allele-specific methylation using BAM and VCF files, calculate derived ASM, and find DAMEs.
workflows.stages: 1. Extract allele-based methylation calls using extract_bams() ;; 2. Summarize methylation calls across samples using calc_derivedasm() ;; 3. Define design matrix and find DAMEs using find_dames()
workflows.code:
bam_files <- c(system.file("extdata", "NORM1_chr19_trim.bam", 
                           package = "DAMEfinder"),
               system.file("extdata", "CRC1_chr19_trim.bam", 
                           package = "DAMEfinder"))

vcf_files <- c(system.file("extdata", "NORM1.chr19.trim.vcf", 
                           package = "DAMEfinder"),
               system.file("extdata", "CRC1.chr19.trim.vcf", 
                           package = "DAMEfinder"))

sample_names <- c("NORM1", "CRC1")

#Use another reference file for demonstration, and fix the seqnames
genome <- BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19
seqnames(genome) <- gsub("chr","",seqnames(genome))
reference_file <- DNAStringSet(genome[[19]], use.names = TRUE)
names(reference_file) <- 19

#Extract reads and extract methylation according to allele
snp.list <- extract_bams(bam_files, vcf_files, sample_names, reference_file,
                       coverage = 2)

derASM <- calc_derivedasm(snp.list)

#We remove all CpG sites with any NA values, but not 0s
filt <- rowSums(!is.na(assay(derASM, "der.ASM"))) == 8 
derASM <- derASM[filt,]

#set the design matrix
grp <- factor(c(rep("CRC",4),rep("NORM",4)), levels = c("NORM", "CRC"))
mod <- model.matrix(~grp)

#Run default
dames <- find_dames(derASM, mod)

#Run empirical method
dames <- find_dames(derASM, mod, pvalAssign = "empirical")

workflows.name: tuple_based_dame_detection
workflows.intent: Read methtuple outputs, calculate tuple-based ASM scores, and find DAMEs without SNP information.
workflows.stages: 1. Read methtuple files using read_tuples() ;; 2. Calculate ASM scores using calc_asm() ;; 3. Define design matrix and find DAMEs using find_dames()
workflows.code:
tuple_files <- c(system.file("extdata", "NORM1_chr19.qs.CG.2.tsv.gz", 
                             package = "DAMEfinder"),
                 system.file("extdata", "CRC1_chr19.qs.CG.2.tsv.gz", 
                             package = "DAMEfinder"))

sample_names <- c("NORM1", "CRC1")

tuple_list <- read_tuples(tuple_files, sample_names)

ASM_mat <- calc_asm(tuple_list)

#load package data
data(readtuples_output)

#run calc_asm and filter object
ASMscore <- calc_asm(readtuples_output)
filt <- rowSums(!is.na(assay(ASMscore, "asm"))) == 5 #filt to avoid warnings
ASMscore <- ASMscore[filt,]

#make design matrix (or specify a contrast)
grp <- factor(c(rep("CRC",3),rep("NORM",2)), levels = c("NORM", "CRC"))
mod <- model.matrix(~grp)

#run default and increase maxGap to get longer, more sparse regions
dames <- find_dames(ASMscore, mod, maxGap = 300)

#run alternative mode
dames <- find_dames(ASMscore, mod,  maxGap = 300, pvalAssign = "empirical")

workflows.name: methyl_circle_visualization
workflows.intent: Visualize the methylation state of individual reads overlapping a specific SNP or CpG site.
workflows.stages: 1. Define SNP or CpG site as a GRanges object ;; 2. Plot methyl-circle plot using methyl_circle_plot() or methyl_circle_plotCpG()
workflows.code:
#put SNP in GRanges (you can find the SNP with the dame_track function)
snp <- GRanges(19, IRanges(267039, width = 1)) #always set the width if your 
#GRanges has 1 site

bam.file <- system.file("extdata", "CRC1_chr19_trim.bam", 
                        package = "DAMEfinder")

vcf.file <- system.file("extdata", "CRC1.chr19.trim.vcf", 
                        package = "DAMEfinder")

methyl_circle_plot(snp = snp, vcfFile = vcf.file, bamFile = bam.file, 
                   refFile = reference_file)

cpgsite <- GRanges(19, IRanges(266998, width = 1))

methyl_circle_plot(snp = snp, vcfFile = vcf.file, bamFile = bam.file, 
                   refFile = reference_file, cpgsite = cpgsite)

methyl_circle_plotCpG(cpgsite = cpgsite, bamFile = bam.file, 
                      refFile = reference_file)

#a random region
dame <- GRanges(19, IRanges(266998,267100))

methyl_circle_plot(snp = snp, vcfFile = vcf.file, bamFile = bam.file, 
                   refFile = reference_file, dame = dame)
